newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish finance ministry sees 3.6 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: Finnish finance ministry sees 3.6 pct growth.

text.p: The pace of Finnish economic growth is expected to remain strong next year, the finance ministry said in a new forecast on Monday, projecting 1998 GDP growth of 3.6 percent. It said consumer prices would rise two percent next year.

The ministry slightly revised its forecasts for this year made in February, cutting the growth forecast to 4.5 percent from 4.6 percent, and the consumer price rise forecast to 1.0 percent from 1.2 percent.
"The growth in total output is expected to continue to be strong next year," it said.
"As the output growth will be focused to a large extent on labour intensive service areas and construction, employment will show a marked increase," the ministry said.
Its 1998 unemployment rate forecast was 13.0 percent, and it cut its earlier 1997 jobless rate forecast by 0.5 percentage points to 14.4 percent.
A jobless rate of 13.0 percent would mean 330,000 unemployed, it said. In April, the unemployment rate was 16.6 percent and the number of unemployed 424,000, Statistics Finland reported last week.
Looking at 1998, the finance ministry said favourable trends in the international economy offered good prospects for Finnish exports.
"As the competitiveness of Finnish exports is expected to further improve slightly, the growth in exports will continue to be brisk," it said.

The increase in private consumption would be slower than this year's projected 3.8 percent while private investment would "still show a considerable increase because of the rapid rise in residential construction," it said.

Summing up the outlook for 1997-98, the ministry said: "The economy is in many respects in balance; all the demand components are growing, employment is showing a marked increase and there are no significant inflationary pressures."
